notes.text: Before Eli — That is, under his inspection and direction. Word - The word of prophecy, or the Revelation of God's will to and by the prophets. Precious - Rare or scarce, such things being most precious in mens' esteem, whereas common things are generally despised. Open vision - God did not impart his Mind by way of vision or Revelation openly, or to any public person, to whom others might resort for satisfaction, though he might privately reveal himself to some pious persons for their particular direction. This is premised, as a reason why Samuel understood not, when God called him once or twice.
His place — In the court of the tabernacle.
Went out — Before the lights of the golden candlestick were put out in the morning.

Did not know — He was not acquainted with God in that extraordinary or prophetical way. And this ignorance of Samuel's served God's design, that his simplicity might give Eli the better assurance of the truth of God's call, and message to Samuel.

Came and stood — Before, he spake to him at a distance, even from the holy oracle between the cherubim: but now, to prevent all farther mistake, the voice came near to him, as if the person speaking had been standing near him.

glossa.text:
*The lamp.* ((ID.)) Which burned in the tabernacle before the light of day. For under the light of day it was quenched, but it shone until the morning; or this signifies that Heli should remain in blindness until he were utterly quenched together with his offspring, that is, should die.

But mystically the blindness of Heli signifies the blindness of the Jews, who acknowledged not the Saviour present, nor the brightness of his miracles, nor his teaching, until the priesthood together with the people and the temple was overthrown.

notes.text: Afar off — Thou knowest what my thoughts will be in such and such circumstances, long before I know it, yea from all eternity.
Compassest — Thou discernest every step I take. It is a metaphor from soldiers besieging their enemies, and setting watches round about them.
Beset me — With thy all-seeing providence. And laid - Thou keepest me, as it were with a strong hand, in thy sight and under thy power.
I cannot — Apprehend in what manner thou dost so presently know all things.

glossa.text: *Unto the end, a psalm of David* *Ddvid**.* ((CASS.)) A psalm full of the depth of mysteries, etc., *as far as* veiled in the prophets, manifest in the Gospel. ((AUG.)) The whole Christ speaks, as one entire man, etc., *as far as* as two in one flesh. *Lord, thou hast proved me.* ((CASS.)) First, concerning the knowledge of God, etc., *as far as* fourthly, how the wicked do him no hurt, there, *If thou wilt kill, O God,* etc. *Lord, thou hast proved.* ((AUG.)) Now restored in Jerusalem, etc., *as far as* this is the person of the whole of human nature returning.

*Thou hast understood.* ((CASS.)) The foreknowledge of the Godhead is here shown, etc., *as far as* because the manhood assumed cannot be made equal to the divine substance. *From afar off.* ((AUG.)) While I am still on pilgrimage, before I come to the fatherland, as the father ran to meet the younger son returning, because he understood his thoughts from afar off, because he had said within himself, worn out with want *egestare*: *I will arise and go to my father.*

*My path,* namely the evil one, by which I went, forsaking my father.

*And the line.* (Otherwise) the boundary, how far I came: far indeed had I gone, but thou wast there. He speaks as a fugitive caught, the vengeance of God following after him.

*And all my ways:* before I went in them; and thou didst permit me to go in labour, that I might return if I would not labour: this I confess. *For there is no guile in my tongue:* now I have justified in thy grace.

My *last things,* when I fed the swine, *The old things,* when I asked for the portion of the substance: this according to the parable. But mystically, *The old things,* when through the ancient sin *pecatum* we fell: *The last things,* the penalty, when we came into this mortality, which is the last, if we are willing to return; otherwise the eternal remains. *Thou hast formed me,* unto labours, unto which we are all born. *Thou hast laid.* (Otherwise) Thou hast made heavy the hand, the avenging hand, weighing down the proud man wholesomely, that it may raise up the humble man, in the hand made heavy.

*Wonderful,* and incomprehensible *incomprehensibllis* to me. *Thy knowledge is become.* It is not easy for me to contemplate thee, whom in my pride I forsook, as it was before, when I was with thee, when I said, give me the portion of the substance. *From me,* that is, from my sin.

*It is strengthened,* (otherwise) it has prevailed. *And I shall not be able* to attain to it of myself. ((AUG.)) In Exodus it is read that the Lord, etc., *as far as* I am not hidden from thee, whose boundary thou seest.

notes.text: For — The fault is not in us, neither in the doctrine they hear from us. We preach not ourselves - As able either to enlighten, or pardon, or sanctify you. But Jesus Christ - As your only wisdom, righteousness, sanctification. And ourselves your servants - Ready to do the meanest offices. For Jesus' sake - Not for honour, interest, or pleasure.

For God hath shined in our hearts — The hearts of all those whom the God of this world no longer blinds. God who is himself our light; not only the author of light, but also the fountain of it. To enlighten us with the knowledge of the glory of God - Of his glorious love, and of his glorious image. In the face of Jesus Christ - Which reflects his glory in another manner than the face of Moses did.

But we — Not only the apostles, but all true believers. Have this treasure - Of divine light, love, glory. In earthen vessels - In frail, feeble, perishing bodies. He proceeds to show, that afflictions, yea, death itself, are so far from hindering the ministration of the Spirit, that they even further it, sharpen the ministers, and increase the fruit. That the excellence of the power, which works these in us, may undeniably appear to be of God.

We are troubled, &c. — The four articles in this verse respect inward, the four in the next outward, afflictions. In each clause the former part shows the "earthen vessels;" the latter, "the excellence of the power." Not crushed - Not swallowed up in care and anxiety. Perplexed - What course to take, but never despairing of his power and love to carry us through.

Always — Wherever we go. Bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus - Continually expecting to lay down our lives like him. That the life also of Jesus might be manifested in our body - That we may also rise and be glorified like him.

For we who yet live — Who are not yet killed for the testimony of Jesus. Are always delivered unto death - Are perpetually in the very jaws of destruction; which we willingly submit to, that we may "obtain a better resurrection."
So then death worketh in us, but life in you — You live in peace; we die daily. Yet - Living or dying, so long as we believe, we cannot but speak.

glossa.text: *For we preach not ourselves.* As if he should say: I speak well unto the glory of Christ, or: We have commended ourselves before God in the manifestation of the truth, and we do other such things; and this for Christ's sake.

*Light to shine.* Which was in the separation of the elements. For darkness began from the time when the confused mass of heaven and earth began to be: afterwards, the light being added, which was done; it is rendered better. In which the disposition of the man who makes progress is signified, whence *you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord ((Ephes. V))*. *In the face of Jesus.* It has this sense: Since the divine nature falls not under sight, it is beheld, so far as is permitted, through the assumed humanity that shines back with the divine light and sends forth lightnings. And hence it is also manifest that God did not send in unbelief, who has abundantly furnished to all the splendour of the light that gives understanding: but they indeed loved unbelief, while he, when they would not look, did not furnish them the ray. *Of the knowledge of the brightness.* The knowledge of the glory of God is that whereby we know that there is a light by which our darkness is enlightened.

*We have.* Thus far he has treated of the height of knowledge: here of the frailty of the flesh, which is unto glory, although it seem the contrary. *A treasure.* The mystery of God, which is dispensed to the faithful, is hidden from the faithless; he affirms it to be a treasure.

*Always the mortification,* etc. There is no doubt that in the martyrs Christ is slain, and that in those who suffer for the faith, whether departures, or bonds, or stripes, are the passions of Christ, that his life also may be made manifest in their body. For the sufferings are they which show the merit unto the life to come, which Christ promised, whence the Apostle says in another place: *When I am weak, then am I powerful,* and again: *Through tribulations,* etc. *May be made manifest.* For certain men doubted concerning the resurrection.

*Therefore death,* etc. Because through death we obtain the life of Jesus: therefore death is not useless, but works something great in us. But the life wherein you delight in earthly things works in you eternal death. Or else, then, passively, that is, for the hope of the life of Jesus death is wrought, that is, by the aforesaid sufferings it is effected in us, that is, we permit it to be effected: but through this, life is effected in you, that is, faith is planted.

notes.text: Matt. xii, 1; Luke vi, 1.

In the days of Abiathar the high priest — Abimelech, the father of Abiathar, was high priest then; Abiathar himself not till some time after. This phrase therefore only means, In the time of Abiathar, who was afterward the high priest. 1 Sam. xxi, 6.
The Sabbath was made for man — And therefore must give way to man's necessity.

Moreover the Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath — Being the supreme Lawgiver, he hath power to dispense with his own laws; and with this in particular. He entered again into the synagogue - At Capernaum on the same day. Matt. xii, 9; Luke vi, 6.
And they — The scribes and Pharisees, watched him, that they might accuse him - Pride, anger, and shame, after being so often put to silence, began now to ripen into malice.
Is it lawful to save life or to kill? — Which he knew they were seeking occasion to do. But they held their peace - Being confounded, though not convinced.

Looking round upon them with anger, being grieved — Angry at the sin, grieved at the sinner; the true standard of Christian anger. But who can separate anger at sin from anger at the sinner? None but a true believer in Christ.
The Pharisees going out — Probably leaving the scribes to watch him still: took counsel with the Herodians - as bitter as they usually were against each other.

glossa.text:
*When on the sabbath days. ((BEDA.))* Note first that the apostles do away with the letter of the sabbath against the Ebionites, who, though they receive the other disciples, repudiate Paul as a transgressor of the law.

*And to pluck the ears of corn.* They hunger as men, having no space for eating because of the crowd. But they set forth an example of a more austere life, they seek not prepared feasts, but simple ones.

((BEDA.)) The disciples pass through the corn, when prelates look upon their subjects with holy solicitude, and how they may draw each one to the faith, diligently, etc., *as far as* this the Lord of the sabbath approves, the foolish defenders of the sabbath disapprove, who love only the surface of the letter, know not the refreshment of the mind, are not acquainted with the rest of souls.

*Have you never read,* etc. Before all others he brings David forward into the midst, who could seem to have opposed the sanctity of the law. And he does this with the design that, through the honour and reverence which they paid to David, he may check the shameless slander which they maliciously aimed at the apostles. As if he should say: Do you not remember that David was bound by the servitude of the law? But I, though I be called the Son of man, am the Lord of the sabbath.

*Under Abiathar,* etc. Let it not trouble thee that others say Achimelech, for both were then present there. Achimelech the father, and Abrathar the son: who, when his father had been slain by Saul, was made the companion of David's exile, and, in his reign, high priest of greater name than his father: and therefore worthy that the Lord should make mention of him, as of a high priest, even while his father was living.

*The loaves of proposition. ((BEDA.))* As if he should say: If David and Achimelech are not blamed by us, but are excused for hunger's sake, why do you condemn in these the cause which in the rest you approve? although it be, etc., *as far as* and all the sons of the Church are priests, joined into a holy priesthood, offering themselves as spiritual sacrifices to God.

*And he gave to them.* Following this. *I will mercy, and not sacrifice ((Ose. VI))*: he judged it better to free men from the peril of famine than to offer sacrifice. The victim well-pleasing to God is the salvation of men.
*Man for the sabbath. ((BEDA.))* The sabbath is so commanded to be kept, that if there be necessity, he is not guilty, etc., *as far as* if a sick man break the fast, he is not held guilty.

*Therefore the Lord.* As if he should say: If David the king and the priests (according to another evangelist), violating the sabbath because of the ministry of the temple, are free from crime, how much more the Son of man, the true King and Priest! and therefore the Lord of the sabbath is not held guilty of the crime of the ears of corn plucked on the sabbath.

*The withered hand. ((BEDA.))* Which was stretched out to the forbidden fruit, and withered from good work, and was restored by the sap of good works through the hands of Christ stretched out upon the cross.

((HIER.)) This man signifies the covetous, who, unwilling to give, wish to receive, to plunder and not to bestow: to whom it is said that they should stretch forth their hands, that is, he who *stole, let him now steal no more, but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have wherewith to give to him that suffereth need ((Ephes. IV))*.

*And they watched him. ((BEDA.))* Because he had plausibly excused the disciples: they watch himself, that if he heal on the sabbath they may accuse him of transgression: if he heal not, of cruelty or of weakness.

*It is lawful to do good on the sabbath days. ((ID.))* He shows that they violate the precepts of the law by a wicked interpretation, thinking that on the sabbath one must keep holiday from good, whereas the law says, etc., *as far as* he set before them the likeness of the sheep, and concluded that *it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.*

*A soul. ((ID.))* By the part he signifies the whole man. Either because he did this for the soul's sake, or because this healing of the hand signifies the salvation of the soul.

*To destroy. ((ID.))* Not that he who is supremely merciful could destroy anyone, but for him not to save is to destroy. As he is said to have hardened the heart of Pharao, not that he hardened it, but that he did not soften it when it was hardened.

*Stretch forth thy hand. ((BEDA.))* The unfruitful weakness of the soul is not better healed than by the bestowing of alms; whence: *He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none: and he that hath meat, let him do in like manner ((Luc. III))*. And in Ecclesiasticus: *Son, let not thy hand be stretched out to take, and shut to give ((Eccl. IV))*. For in vain does he spread out his hands to the Lord in prayer, who does not stretch them out to the widow that asks.

*And the hand was restored unto him.* A great zeal of wickedness, they reckon it for a crime., that at his word the hand was healed. Nor even on the sabbath can he be convicted of having laboured, who spoke and they were made: whereas they themselves on the sabbath carry food, hand round cups, and the rest that is necessary for living.

*And going forth.* They who cannot do it by themselves seek companions of iniquity. *With the Herodians.* The ministers of Herod, because of the enmities which he himself was exercising against the man, pursued with snares and hatreds Jesus, whom John preached.

echoes.text: Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
echoes.note: The 'god of this world has blinded the minds' so they cannot see the light recasts Isaiah's hardening commission, where eyes are made blind 'lest they see.' High recurrence in Paul (Rom 11:8) and strong coherence with the veiling theme of ch. 3 support a deliberate allusion.

echoes.text: God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
echoes.note: Calling Christ 'the image of God' reads the creation of humanity in God's image figurally, with Christ as the true eikon. The pairing of image (4:4) and the creation of light (4:6) keys the whole pericope to Genesis 1, making this a deliberate new-creation typology.

echoes.text: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
echoes.note: 'God who said, Light will shine out of darkness' rewords the creation fiat, presenting conversion as a new act of creation in the heart. The volume is high (clear verbal evocation of the fiat lux) and coherent with the Genesis 1 image motif of 4:4.

echoes.text: But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
echoes.note: Deuteronomy's lament that the LORD had 'not given a heart to know, eyes to see' supplies the unbelief-as-imposed-blindness motif Paul fuses with Isaiah. Paul cites this very verse in Rom 11:8, raising its availability and coherence here.

echoes.text: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: The Servant's task to 'open blind eyes' frames Paul's gospel as the light that should dawn; 42:19's 'blind servant' sharpens the irony of unbelieving blindness. Volume is moderate but coherence with the Isaianic light/blindness cluster Paul is mining is strong.

echoes.text: For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, And an unspotted mirror of the working of God, And an image of his goodness.
echoes.note: Wisdom as 'image of his goodness' and radiance of glory is the Second-Temple lexicon for Christ as 'image of God' and 'glory of Christ.' Availability and coherence are high; volume rests on shared eikon/glory vocabulary rather than a quotation.

echoes.text: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of Yahweh’s glory, as the waters cover the sea.
echoes.note: 'The light of the knowledge of the glory of God' closely tracks Habakkuk's promise that the earth will be filled with 'the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.' The triple chain knowledge-glory-LORD is distinctive enough to register as more than coincidence.

echoes.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: Light shining on those in darkness echoes Isaiah's people who 'walked in darkness' seeing a great light, reinforcing the gospel-as-dawn imagery. Coherent with the Isaianic light theme already in play, though the verbal contact is general.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.
echoes.note: 'The glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ' continues ch. 3's contrast with the glory on Moses' face, transferring the shining-face motif to Christ. Recurrence from the immediately prior argument makes the Exodus glory narrative the controlling subtext.

echoes.text: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!
echoes.note: 'Precious sons of Zion' reckoned as 'earthen pots, the work of the potter' supplies the exact pairing of priceless worth held in cheap clay vessels that Paul exploits. The treasure/earthen-vessel antithesis gives this strong coherence and notable volume.

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: The 'clay vessel' housing divine power evokes the human creature formed from dust and animated by God's breath, so the frailty is constitutive of creaturehood. Figural rather than verbal, but it grounds Paul's 'not from ourselves' in the dust-origin of humanity.

echoes.text: But now, Yahweh, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.
echoes.note: 'We are the clay, you our potter' establishes the creature-as-vessel theme that Paul presses to magnify God's power over human weakness. Availability and coherence are strong within Paul's potter/clay usage (Rom 9:21).

echoes.text: He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all of them trumpets, and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.
echoes.note: Gideon's torches hidden in clay jars, broken to flash God's deliverance, joins the light of 4:6 to the clay vessels of 4:7: divine power shines precisely when the fragile jar is shattered. The shared jar+light+power configuration gives this a striking coherence.

echoes.text: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
echoes.note: Those who 'dwell in houses of clay' and are easily crushed parallel the fragility of the clay vessel motif. Volume is faint and the contact is conceptual, so it functions only as a supporting echo.

echoes.text: Yah has punished me severely, but he has not given me over to death.
echoes.note: 'Struck down, yet not destroyed' closely matches the psalmist's 'the LORD has chastened me severely, but has not given me over to death.' The structure of severe affliction stopped just short of destruction is the same, supplying good volume for the climactic clause.

echoes.text: Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahweh holds him up with his hand.
echoes.note: 'Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down, for the LORD upholds his hand' mirrors the not-forsaken/not-destroyed paradox of the righteous sufferer. Coherent with Paul's hardship-catalog theology of divine sustenance.

echoes.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
echoes.note: 'Pursued, yet not forsaken' echoes the covenant assurance that God 'will not leave you nor forsake you.' The phrase is widespread, so volume is low and the link is a general scriptural commonplace.

echoes.text: Yes, for your sake we are killed all day long. We are regarded as sheep for the slaughter.
echoes.note: 'Always delivered to death for Jesus' sake' anticipates the very verse ('we are killed all day long') Paul quotes at Rom 8:36, casting apostolic suffering as the lot of the faithful slain for God. Recurrence in Paul lends the echo weight.

echoes.text: Yet it pleased Yahweh to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed. He shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of Yahweh shall prosper in his hand.
echoes.note: Carrying 'the putting to death of Jesus' so that 'life may be revealed' loosely figures the Servant whose death yields life and offspring. The contact is thematic and contested, with no verbal tether, hence figural and low.

notes.text: Keep the sabbath-day, to sanctify it — Dost thou do no work on this day, which can be done as well on another? Art thou peculiarly careful on this day, to avoid all conversation, which does not tend to the knowledge and love of God? Dost thou watch narrowly over all that are within thy gates, that they too may keep it holy? And dost thou try every possible means, to bring all men, wherever you are, to do the same?

Joseph — Among the people of Israel. Testimony - For a witness of that glorious deliverance. He - God. Went - As a captain at the head of his people. Egypt - To execute his judgments upon that land. I - My progenitors, for all the successive generations of Israel make one body, and are sometimes spoken of as one person. A language - The Egyptian language, which at first was unknown to the Israelites, Gen. xlii, 13, and probably continued so for some considerable time, because they were much separated both in place and conversation from the Egyptians.
Pots — This word denotes all those vessels wherein they carried water, straw, lime, or bricks.
Calledst — At the Red Sea. Secret place - From the dark and cloudy pillar, whence I thundered against the Egyptians.
Testify — This God did presently after he brought them from Meribah, even at Sinai.
Wide — Either to pray for mercies, or to receive the mercies which I am ready to give you.

glossa.text: *He rejoiceth in God.* Asaph, having set before himself the image of a certain solemnity, stirs up the elect to the festival.

*Take a psalm.* ((AUG.)) The words of God, that human acts may come together into one fellowship: for this is the peace of Jerusalem, this is the reckoning of what is given and what is received; whence the Apostle: *If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things ((I Cor. IX))*.

*Blow the trumpet.* ((AUG.)) Thus far, up to the division, these things are to be taken either according to the letter, simply of the Jews, or allegorically of Christians. ((AUG.)) *Blow the trumpet,* and declare, etc., *as far as* whence Isaias: *Cry, cease not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet,* etc. *On the new moon with the trumpet.* ((CASS.)) At the beginning of the month the Jews were bidden to sound the trumpet, that is, at the beginning of the new moon, which is also called the feast of trumpets, which they celebrated in memory of that thing, that the Lord showed Abraham the ram sticking among the briers, which he offered up in the place of Isaac.
*For it is a commandment in Israel; and a judgment,* etc. ((ID.)) Therefore the trumpet must be sounded, because the law was given to the Jews through Moses, and because he is to be their judge.
*In Joseph.* ((AUG.)) The Gentiles are Joseph, etc., *as far as* where he ought to have had a heart.

*From the burdens.* ((AUG.)) By what burdens: *hands in the basket,* that is, by servile work. Sins are servile works, according to that saying: *Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin ((Joan. VIII))*. *They served in the basket. ((ID.))* In the uncleannesses of sins, in earthly and miry works.

*In tribulation,* etc. ((CASS.)) So the Prophet: the Lord turns aside, saying, *In tribulation,* the benefits of God are reckoned to them, that the offence may be judged the heavier. *I heard thee in the secret place.* ((AUG.)) That with the heart thou mayest believe unto justice. *I proved thee,* that with the mouth confession may be made unto salvation. *Of the storm,* etc. Not in the storm of the sea, but of the heart: where he that is heard must be proved, in the water of contradiction: for he that already walks the way of God has men withstanding him in many ways. This is the water of contradiction, which the ancients felt, but now it is well dried up: for then the waters of the peoples were troubled, and resisted fiercely. Then to Samson, that strong man, that is, to Christ, going to take a wife from among the strangers, that is, the Church from among the Gentiles, there met a roaring lion, that is, the people of the Gentiles, but he tore him in pieces as a kid of the goats: and because that roaring people was nothing but a sickly sinner. But when that fierceness had been slain in him, he no longer roars so; nay, in that very people we now find laws in favour of the Church, as it were a honeycomb in the mouth of the lion. *The water of contradiction.* Christ was so even in himself, as it was said of him when he was born: *This one shall be unto the ruin, and the resurrection of many, for a sign which shall be contradicted ((Luc. II))* , as the Jews contradicted the title of the cross.

*Hear, O my people.* ((CASS.)) Diapsalma. Thus far of the oil of the winepresses, now of the lees, which is said by way of warning; here the reprobate are reproved. *I will testify unto thee.* The Lord himself makes himself the witness of the judgment of truth, both here and in the world to come, that none may doubt. Then he adds what he would have him understand: Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me; and by calling him Israel he signifies one familiar to himself, and invites him to his commands. *In thee,* in thy heart, where truth, not falsehood, ought to be. *New,* lest the Word of the Father be thought to be under time. *A strange god,* one that is such in name, not in essence. *Strange:* It is well-nigh an equal crime to think God new, and to serve idols.

*There shall be no new god in thee, neither,* etc. ((AUG.)) Some make themselves new gods, either idols, or a Christ unequal to the Father, and feign other such things in the heart: and so in all of them earthly thought is the temple of idols; the opinion is various, the vanity one. Therefore Samson bound together the tails of the foxes, that he might set fire to the harvests of the Philistines. Samson is interpreted *their sun,* namely of those to whom he himself shines, not of all: of whom the wicked shall say: *We have erred from the way of truth, and the sun of justice hath not shined upon us ((Sap. V))* . And elsewhere: *He is the sun of justice, and health is in his wings ((Malac. IV))*. The foxes are the treacherous, and most of all the heretics, lurking in winding caverns, deceiving, stinking with their smell: who, although they seem to disagree with one another, yet agree in evil, that is, in their hinder parts, and are held by a like vanity, and burn the harvests, not of our own, because God knows who are his, but of the strangers, which are vessels of dishonour.
*Who brought thee out.* God is pointed out by his own deeds.

notes.text: For — The fault is not in us, neither in the doctrine they hear from us. We preach not ourselves - As able either to enlighten, or pardon, or sanctify you. But Jesus Christ - As your only wisdom, righteousness, sanctification. And ourselves your servants - Ready to do the meanest offices. For Jesus' sake - Not for honour, interest, or pleasure.

For God hath shined in our hearts — The hearts of all those whom the God of this world no longer blinds. God who is himself our light; not only the author of light, but also the fountain of it. To enlighten us with the knowledge of the glory of God - Of his glorious love, and of his glorious image. In the face of Jesus Christ - Which reflects his glory in another manner than the face of Moses did.

But we — Not only the apostles, but all true believers. Have this treasure - Of divine light, love, glory. In earthen vessels - In frail, feeble, perishing bodies. He proceeds to show, that afflictions, yea, death itself, are so far from hindering the ministration of the Spirit, that they even further it, sharpen the ministers, and increase the fruit. That the excellence of the power, which works these in us, may undeniably appear to be of God.

We are troubled, &c. — The four articles in this verse respect inward, the four in the next outward, afflictions. In each clause the former part shows the "earthen vessels;" the latter, "the excellence of the power." Not crushed - Not swallowed up in care and anxiety. Perplexed - What course to take, but never despairing of his power and love to carry us through.

Always — Wherever we go. Bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus - Continually expecting to lay down our lives like him. That the life also of Jesus might be manifested in our body - That we may also rise and be glorified like him.

For we who yet live — Who are not yet killed for the testimony of Jesus. Are always delivered unto death - Are perpetually in the very jaws of destruction; which we willingly submit to, that we may "obtain a better resurrection."
So then death worketh in us, but life in you — You live in peace; we die daily. Yet - Living or dying, so long as we believe, we cannot but speak.

glossa.text: *For we preach not ourselves.* As if he should say: I speak well unto the glory of Christ, or: We have commended ourselves before God in the manifestation of the truth, and we do other such things; and this for Christ's sake.

*Light to shine.* Which was in the separation of the elements. For darkness began from the time when the confused mass of heaven and earth began to be: afterwards, the light being added, which was done; it is rendered better. In which the disposition of the man who makes progress is signified, whence *you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord ((Ephes. V))*. *In the face of Jesus.* It has this sense: Since the divine nature falls not under sight, it is beheld, so far as is permitted, through the assumed humanity that shines back with the divine light and sends forth lightnings. And hence it is also manifest that God did not send in unbelief, who has abundantly furnished to all the splendour of the light that gives understanding: but they indeed loved unbelief, while he, when they would not look, did not furnish them the ray. *Of the knowledge of the brightness.* The knowledge of the glory of God is that whereby we know that there is a light by which our darkness is enlightened.

*We have.* Thus far he has treated of the height of knowledge: here of the frailty of the flesh, which is unto glory, although it seem the contrary. *A treasure.* The mystery of God, which is dispensed to the faithful, is hidden from the faithless; he affirms it to be a treasure.

*Always the mortification,* etc. There is no doubt that in the martyrs Christ is slain, and that in those who suffer for the faith, whether departures, or bonds, or stripes, are the passions of Christ, that his life also may be made manifest in their body. For the sufferings are they which show the merit unto the life to come, which Christ promised, whence the Apostle says in another place: *When I am weak, then am I powerful,* and again: *Through tribulations,* etc. *May be made manifest.* For certain men doubted concerning the resurrection.

*Therefore death,* etc. Because through death we obtain the life of Jesus: therefore death is not useless, but works something great in us. But the life wherein you delight in earthly things works in you eternal death. Or else, then, passively, that is, for the hope of the life of Jesus death is wrought, that is, by the aforesaid sufferings it is effected in us, that is, we permit it to be effected: but through this, life is effected in you, that is, faith is planted.

notes.text: Matt. xii, 1; Luke vi, 1.

In the days of Abiathar the high priest — Abimelech, the father of Abiathar, was high priest then; Abiathar himself not till some time after. This phrase therefore only means, In the time of Abiathar, who was afterward the high priest. 1 Sam. xxi, 6.
The Sabbath was made for man — And therefore must give way to man's necessity.

Moreover the Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath — Being the supreme Lawgiver, he hath power to dispense with his own laws; and with this in particular. He entered again into the synagogue - At Capernaum on the same day. Matt. xii, 9; Luke vi, 6.
And they — The scribes and Pharisees, watched him, that they might accuse him - Pride, anger, and shame, after being so often put to silence, began now to ripen into malice.
Is it lawful to save life or to kill? — Which he knew they were seeking occasion to do. But they held their peace - Being confounded, though not convinced.

Looking round upon them with anger, being grieved — Angry at the sin, grieved at the sinner; the true standard of Christian anger. But who can separate anger at sin from anger at the sinner? None but a true believer in Christ.
The Pharisees going out — Probably leaving the scribes to watch him still: took counsel with the Herodians - as bitter as they usually were against each other.

glossa.text:
*When on the sabbath days. ((BEDA.))* Note first that the apostles do away with the letter of the sabbath against the Ebionites, who, though they receive the other disciples, repudiate Paul as a transgressor of the law.

*And to pluck the ears of corn.* They hunger as men, having no space for eating because of the crowd. But they set forth an example of a more austere life, they seek not prepared feasts, but simple ones.

((BEDA.)) The disciples pass through the corn, when prelates look upon their subjects with holy solicitude, and how they may draw each one to the faith, diligently, etc., *as far as* this the Lord of the sabbath approves, the foolish defenders of the sabbath disapprove, who love only the surface of the letter, know not the refreshment of the mind, are not acquainted with the rest of souls.

*Have you never read,* etc. Before all others he brings David forward into the midst, who could seem to have opposed the sanctity of the law. And he does this with the design that, through the honour and reverence which they paid to David, he may check the shameless slander which they maliciously aimed at the apostles. As if he should say: Do you not remember that David was bound by the servitude of the law? But I, though I be called the Son of man, am the Lord of the sabbath.

*Under Abiathar,* etc. Let it not trouble thee that others say Achimelech, for both were then present there. Achimelech the father, and Abrathar the son: who, when his father had been slain by Saul, was made the companion of David's exile, and, in his reign, high priest of greater name than his father: and therefore worthy that the Lord should make mention of him, as of a high priest, even while his father was living.

*The loaves of proposition. ((BEDA.))* As if he should say: If David and Achimelech are not blamed by us, but are excused for hunger's sake, why do you condemn in these the cause which in the rest you approve? although it be, etc., *as far as* and all the sons of the Church are priests, joined into a holy priesthood, offering themselves as spiritual sacrifices to God.

*And he gave to them.* Following this. *I will mercy, and not sacrifice ((Ose. VI))*: he judged it better to free men from the peril of famine than to offer sacrifice. The victim well-pleasing to God is the salvation of men.
*Man for the sabbath. ((BEDA.))* The sabbath is so commanded to be kept, that if there be necessity, he is not guilty, etc., *as far as* if a sick man break the fast, he is not held guilty.

*Therefore the Lord.* As if he should say: If David the king and the priests (according to another evangelist), violating the sabbath because of the ministry of the temple, are free from crime, how much more the Son of man, the true King and Priest! and therefore the Lord of the sabbath is not held guilty of the crime of the ears of corn plucked on the sabbath.

*The withered hand. ((BEDA.))* Which was stretched out to the forbidden fruit, and withered from good work, and was restored by the sap of good works through the hands of Christ stretched out upon the cross.

((HIER.)) This man signifies the covetous, who, unwilling to give, wish to receive, to plunder and not to bestow: to whom it is said that they should stretch forth their hands, that is, he who *stole, let him now steal no more, but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have wherewith to give to him that suffereth need ((Ephes. IV))*.

*And they watched him. ((BEDA.))* Because he had plausibly excused the disciples: they watch himself, that if he heal on the sabbath they may accuse him of transgression: if he heal not, of cruelty or of weakness.

*It is lawful to do good on the sabbath days. ((ID.))* He shows that they violate the precepts of the law by a wicked interpretation, thinking that on the sabbath one must keep holiday from good, whereas the law says, etc., *as far as* he set before them the likeness of the sheep, and concluded that *it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.*

*A soul. ((ID.))* By the part he signifies the whole man. Either because he did this for the soul's sake, or because this healing of the hand signifies the salvation of the soul.

*To destroy. ((ID.))* Not that he who is supremely merciful could destroy anyone, but for him not to save is to destroy. As he is said to have hardened the heart of Pharao, not that he hardened it, but that he did not soften it when it was hardened.

*Stretch forth thy hand. ((BEDA.))* The unfruitful weakness of the soul is not better healed than by the bestowing of alms; whence: *He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none: and he that hath meat, let him do in like manner ((Luc. III))*. And in Ecclesiasticus: *Son, let not thy hand be stretched out to take, and shut to give ((Eccl. IV))*. For in vain does he spread out his hands to the Lord in prayer, who does not stretch them out to the widow that asks.

*And the hand was restored unto him.* A great zeal of wickedness, they reckon it for a crime., that at his word the hand was healed. Nor even on the sabbath can he be convicted of having laboured, who spoke and they were made: whereas they themselves on the sabbath carry food, hand round cups, and the rest that is necessary for living.

*And going forth.* They who cannot do it by themselves seek companions of iniquity. *With the Herodians.* The ministers of Herod, because of the enmities which he himself was exercising against the man, pursued with snares and hatreds Jesus, whom John preached.

echoes.text: Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
echoes.note: The 'god of this world has blinded the minds' so they cannot see the light recasts Isaiah's hardening commission, where eyes are made blind 'lest they see.' High recurrence in Paul (Rom 11:8) and strong coherence with the veiling theme of ch. 3 support a deliberate allusion.

echoes.text: God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
echoes.note: Calling Christ 'the image of God' reads the creation of humanity in God's image figurally, with Christ as the true eikon. The pairing of image (4:4) and the creation of light (4:6) keys the whole pericope to Genesis 1, making this a deliberate new-creation typology.

echoes.text: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
echoes.note: 'God who said, Light will shine out of darkness' rewords the creation fiat, presenting conversion as a new act of creation in the heart. The volume is high (clear verbal evocation of the fiat lux) and coherent with the Genesis 1 image motif of 4:4.

echoes.text: But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
echoes.note: Deuteronomy's lament that the LORD had 'not given a heart to know, eyes to see' supplies the unbelief-as-imposed-blindness motif Paul fuses with Isaiah. Paul cites this very verse in Rom 11:8, raising its availability and coherence here.

echoes.text: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: The Servant's task to 'open blind eyes' frames Paul's gospel as the light that should dawn; 42:19's 'blind servant' sharpens the irony of unbelieving blindness. Volume is moderate but coherence with the Isaianic light/blindness cluster Paul is mining is strong.

echoes.text: For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, And an unspotted mirror of the working of God, And an image of his goodness.
echoes.note: Wisdom as 'image of his goodness' and radiance of glory is the Second-Temple lexicon for Christ as 'image of God' and 'glory of Christ.' Availability and coherence are high; volume rests on shared eikon/glory vocabulary rather than a quotation.

echoes.text: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of Yahweh’s glory, as the waters cover the sea.
echoes.note: 'The light of the knowledge of the glory of God' closely tracks Habakkuk's promise that the earth will be filled with 'the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.' The triple chain knowledge-glory-LORD is distinctive enough to register as more than coincidence.

echoes.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: Light shining on those in darkness echoes Isaiah's people who 'walked in darkness' seeing a great light, reinforcing the gospel-as-dawn imagery. Coherent with the Isaianic light theme already in play, though the verbal contact is general.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.
echoes.note: 'The glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ' continues ch. 3's contrast with the glory on Moses' face, transferring the shining-face motif to Christ. Recurrence from the immediately prior argument makes the Exodus glory narrative the controlling subtext.

echoes.text: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!
echoes.note: 'Precious sons of Zion' reckoned as 'earthen pots, the work of the potter' supplies the exact pairing of priceless worth held in cheap clay vessels that Paul exploits. The treasure/earthen-vessel antithesis gives this strong coherence and notable volume.

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: The 'clay vessel' housing divine power evokes the human creature formed from dust and animated by God's breath, so the frailty is constitutive of creaturehood. Figural rather than verbal, but it grounds Paul's 'not from ourselves' in the dust-origin of humanity.

echoes.text: But now, Yahweh, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.
echoes.note: 'We are the clay, you our potter' establishes the creature-as-vessel theme that Paul presses to magnify God's power over human weakness. Availability and coherence are strong within Paul's potter/clay usage (Rom 9:21).

echoes.text: He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all of them trumpets, and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.
echoes.note: Gideon's torches hidden in clay jars, broken to flash God's deliverance, joins the light of 4:6 to the clay vessels of 4:7: divine power shines precisely when the fragile jar is shattered. The shared jar+light+power configuration gives this a striking coherence.

echoes.text: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
echoes.note: Those who 'dwell in houses of clay' and are easily crushed parallel the fragility of the clay vessel motif. Volume is faint and the contact is conceptual, so it functions only as a supporting echo.

echoes.text: Yah has punished me severely, but he has not given me over to death.
echoes.note: 'Struck down, yet not destroyed' closely matches the psalmist's 'the LORD has chastened me severely, but has not given me over to death.' The structure of severe affliction stopped just short of destruction is the same, supplying good volume for the climactic clause.

echoes.text: Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahweh holds him up with his hand.
echoes.note: 'Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down, for the LORD upholds his hand' mirrors the not-forsaken/not-destroyed paradox of the righteous sufferer. Coherent with Paul's hardship-catalog theology of divine sustenance.

echoes.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
echoes.note: 'Pursued, yet not forsaken' echoes the covenant assurance that God 'will not leave you nor forsake you.' The phrase is widespread, so volume is low and the link is a general scriptural commonplace.

echoes.text: Yes, for your sake we are killed all day long. We are regarded as sheep for the slaughter.
echoes.note: 'Always delivered to death for Jesus' sake' anticipates the very verse ('we are killed all day long') Paul quotes at Rom 8:36, casting apostolic suffering as the lot of the faithful slain for God. Recurrence in Paul lends the echo weight.

echoes.text: Yet it pleased Yahweh to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed. He shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of Yahweh shall prosper in his hand.
echoes.note: Carrying 'the putting to death of Jesus' so that 'life may be revealed' loosely figures the Servant whose death yields life and offspring. The contact is thematic and contested, with no verbal tether, hence figural and low.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Before a word is on our tongue, O Lord, you know it.
You search us out; you know us through and through.
The lamp of God has not gone out; a boy hears his name in the dark.
Speak, Lord; your servant is listening.
You made the sabbath for us, not us for the sabbath.
Here we lay our burdens down and breathe.
Come, let us worship the God who knows us by name.
We come to listen and obey. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: It is the middle of the night, the lamp of God still flickering, and a voice you almost miss is calling your name.
Speak, Lord; your servant is listening.
There is no dark deep enough to hide you from God; the night is as bright as the day to the One who knit you together.
Speak, Lord; your servant is listening.
You come carrying a long week, hungry as the disciples in the grainfields, and God says the day of rest was made for you.
Speak, Lord; your servant is listening.
So lay down your burden and lift up your head; the One who knows you completely is glad you have come.
Speak, Lord; your servant is listening. Here we are.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The lamp still burns; a voice calls in the dark.
Speak, Lord; we are listening.
You knew our words before we spoke them.
Speak, Lord; we are listening.
The sabbath was made for us; here we rest.
Speak, Lord; we are listening.
Come, let us worship the God who calls us by name.
Speak, Lord; we are listening. Amen.
